ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A minimal pair is two words that (1 mark)
   A. have the same spelling
   B. mean the same thing
   C. rhyme with each other
   D. differ in only one sound

2. What is extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning
   B. Studying one text word by word with the teacher
   C. Copying notes from the board
   D. Reading only for a test

3. Where was Omondi's mother on the day of the story? (1 mark)
   A. At the market
   B. At school
   C. At the clinic getting her medicine
   D. At the barber's

4. Which is a possessive pronoun? (1 mark)
   A. yours
   B. you
   C. yourself
   D. your

5. Which verb is NOT normally used in the progressive form? (1 mark)
   A. know
   B. sing
   C. write
   D. run

6. Which detail uses the sense of smell? (1 mark)
   A. I heard a bell.
   B. I saw a table.
   C. I could smell fresh bread.
   D. I touched a wall.

7. What should you do at a railway crossing? (1 mark)
   A. Run across
   B. Ride faster
   C. Play on the track
   D. Stop, look and listen

8. Which is a fact, not an opinion? (1 mark)
   A. Saving is a good idea.
   B. Everyone should join.
   C. The club meets on Fridays.
   D. The club is the best.

9. Which phrase is a polite way of adding to what someone said? (1 mark)
   A. Be quiet, I am talking
   B. Stop it now
   C. That is wrong
   D. May I add something?

10. What does 'Many hands make light work' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Hands are heavy
   B. Work must be light
   C. A job is easier when many people help
   D. Big hands are strong

11. A reading log helps you to (1 mark)
   A. sell books
   B. hide your books
   C. remember what you have read
   D. break books

12. We answer comprehension questions best in (1 mark)
   A. numbers only
   B. one letter
   C. drawings only
   D. full sentences

13. Intonation: Which word has the long sound /uː/? (1 mark)
   A. good
   B. full
   C. computer
   D. put

14. What is the plural of 'monkey'? (1 mark)
   A. monkeis
   B. monkeys
   C. monkies
   D. monkeyes

15. Which sentence has a comma before the spoken words? (1 mark)
   A. Mother, said "Please close the door."
   B. Mother said, "Please close the door."
   C. Mother said. "Please close the door"
   D. Mother said "Please close the door"

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
16. Write one sentence with 'enough ... to' and one with 'a lot of' about your school. (3 marks)

17. Fill in much or many: (a) How ___ eggs? (b) How ___ sugar? (2 marks)

18. Correct these sentences: (a) Who did scored the goal? (b) When you will come? (3 marks)

19. List the five parts of a friendly letter. (3 marks)

20. Why is it important to use polite words? Give two reasons. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — differ in only one sound
   For example tin and din differ only in the first sound.

2. A — Choosing materials and reading a lot on your own for pleasure and learning
   Extensive reading is wide, independent reading.

3. C — At the clinic getting her medicine
   The story says she was at the clinic.

4. A — yours
   Yours stands alone and shows ownership.

5. A — know
   'Know' describes a state, not an action in progress.

6. C — I could smell fresh bread.
   It describes something smelt.

7. D — Stop, look and listen
   Trains cannot stop quickly.

8. C — The club meets on Fridays.
   A fact can be checked.

9. D — May I add something?
   'May I add something?' asks permission politely.

10. C — A job is easier when many people help
   Sharing work makes it easier.

11. C — remember what you have read
   It records titles, dates and what you liked.

12. D — full sentences
   Full sentences show that we understand.

13. C — computer
   Computer has /uː/ in its second syllable.

14. B — monkeys
   A vowel comes before y, so just add s.

15. B — Mother said, "Please close the door."
   A comma comes after 'said' before the spoken words.

SECTION B
----
16. (3 marks)
   Answer: We have enough desks to seat every learner. The school has a lot of trees.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each pattern and 1 mark for correct punctuation.

17. (2 marks)
   Answer: (a) many (b) much
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

18. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) Who scored the goal? (b) When will you come?
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correction and 1 for question marks and capitals.

19. (3 marks)
   Answer: Address, date, greeting, body, closing and name (address and date may be given together).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 mark for greeting and body, 1 mark for closing and name.

20. (4 marks)
   Answer: Polite words show respect and make people feel welcome. They help people to cooperate and be friendly.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for each reason.
